lots.title: Inspection and Maintenance of Indoor Gymnasium, Fitness and Sport Equipment, and Outdoor Schools Play and Sport Equipment
lots.description: Synthetic single-scope lot representing the undivided framework. ESPO (Leicestershire County Council, trading as ESPO) is establishing a framework agreement (ref. 107_26) for the inspection and maintenance of (a) indoor gymnasium, fitness and sport equipment and (b) outdoor schools play and sport equipment. Contracting is performed by Customers (ESPO plus other PA23 Contracting Authorities identified in the Tender Notice) by call-off with or without further competitive selection. The framework itself does not itemise goods/services, service levels, CPV codes, or technical standards in this document; those are deferred to Framework Schedule 1, which is to be populated from Section 2 of the Invitation to Tender (the Specification) and the Supplier's response to the Statement of Requirements at the point of award.
requirements: Supply inspection and maintenance of the Goods and/or Services in accordance with the (to-be-populated) Framework Schedule 1 Specification and the Supplier's response to the Statement of Requirements.
Provide Goods and/or Services that conform to the Specification and Call-Off Terms (clause 7.5).

Comply with the Standards (British Standards produced by BSI Group, international standards, ESPO internal policies and procedures, and Government codes of practice and guidance referred to in Framework Schedule 1) and with applicable Law (clause 13.2).
Deliver in accordance with the Service Levels set out in Framework Schedule 1 and any minimum Service Levels in the Call-Off Terms (Framework Schedule 10 §3.1, §4.1).
Operate under Procurement Act 2023 (PA23) obligations, including transparency, debarment/excluded supplier checks, and cooperation with Section 78/80 requirements.
Submit accurate and timely Management Information using the MI Reporting Template every Quarter (Framework Schedule 7).
Pay the Framework Fee of 3.5% (Framework Schedule 2 §1.4).
Appoint a nominated Framework Manager and deputy (Framework Schedule 10 §2.1.1).

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Further Competitive Selection Process Award Criteria (applied at call-off)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Framework Schedule 5 states that Customers running a further competitive selection may either reuse ESPO's framework-establishment scheme or notify Suppliers of a revised scheme with different weightings; it explicitly anticipates that because non-price factors were assessed when the framework was established, increased weighting may be given to price at the further competitive stage. Concrete criteria and weightings are not fixed in this document.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Not fixed in this document; set per call-off by the Customer, with increased price weighting anticipated at further competition stage.

evidence_anchor.section_ref: Framework Schedule 5 - Further Competitive Selection Process Award Criteria
evidence_anchor.anchor_text: The following criteria ('the Further Competitive Selection Process Award Criteria') shall be applied to the Further Competitive Selection Process Procedure in Framework Schedule 4

evaluation_criteria.summary: Framework Schedule 4 §2.1 enumerates three objective mechanisms for selecting a Framework Supplier without re-opening competition: (a) cheapest Supplier on Framework Prices, (b) sole Supplier capable of delivering in the geographical location, or (c) Supplier with prior involvement in equivalent Goods/Services in the preceding 12 months where alternative instruction would cause demonstrable inefficiencies or duplication of costs.

evidence_anchor.section_ref: Framework Schedule 4 §2.1 Award Procedure (Call Off Without Competition)
evidence_anchor.anchor_text: To the cheapest Supplier for the Goods and/or Services ... Where only one Supplier can deliver ... Where a Supplier has had prior involvement in the provision of equivalent Goods and/or Services

warnings.message: The procurement is a single-scope framework and is not divided into lots. This skill emits a single synthetic lot (lot_number="1") covering the full framework scope so downstream persistence can attach lot-scoped evidence. Consistent with the published Tender Notice (2026/S 000-002119) and the Background recitals which reference a single framework arrangement.

Framework Schedule 1 explicitly states that the Specification (Section 2 of the Invitation to Tender) and the Supplier's response to the Statement of Requirements (Section 1 of the Tender Submission Document) will be incorporated into this Schedule only after tender evaluation and prior to entry into the Framework Agreement. Therefore this document contains no itemised goods/services list, no service levels, and no KPI targets for specific services.
evidence_refs: Framework Schedule 1 trailing paragraph ('Upon completion of the tender evaluation exercise...')

warnings.message: No product-level requirements, technical attributes, quantities, or SKU-like seeds are itemised in this document. product_requirement_seeds is empty. Downstream product candidate generation will need to pull seeds from the Specification document (Section 2 of the ITT) once available.

No CPV codes are cited in the document text. CPV codes 37400000-2 (Sports goods and equipment) and 50000000-5 (Repair and maintenance services) are present in the upstream notice metadata but do not appear in this document, so cpv_codes on the lot is emitted empty per skill contract (authoritative truth from the tender document only).

No specific British or international standard reference (e.g., no BS EN, EN, ISO, or IEC number) is cited in this document. The only 'Standards' reference is the generic definitional clause pointing to Framework Schedule 1, which is itself deferred. Downstream compliance reasoning should treat technical_standards as pending until the ITT Specification is ingested.

Framework Schedule 5 defines the award scheme abstractly and explicitly defers concrete weighting decisions to each Customer's call-off exercise. No fixed numeric weightings or criterion-score pairs exist in this document.
